source_acquisition.search_note: PDF homepage, footnotes, body and references contain no paper-specific code URL. The inventory row is stale no_public_source_found and no local visual_sources directory exists. GitHub search found ucas-elysia/Faire, whose repository description/README title directly match the paper and whose README calls static/images PNGs figures extracted from the LaTeX source. The tree contains rendered PNG assets and a camera-ready PDF but no editable TeX/TikZ/PGF/SVG figure source, plot scripts, table generators or data files; therefore the status is partial_visual_source. PNG assets were matched against the 200 dpi render for Figures 1–8, 12–17. Figures 9–11 and Tables 1–7 remain PDF-only evidence.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Low-saturation blue statistical charts; sequential blue heatmap; blue/green/orange/pink pipeline and case roles; red denotes failure or RL loss; Table 2 uses cyan Faire-row and green best-cell highlights.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: 正文表格和 prompt/card 文字保留 PDF text/vector objects；统计图、截图和 qualitative panels 混合或栅格嵌入。Embedded raster effective resolution varies substantially (about 70–787 ppi in the PDF object list), so all judgments use the 200 dpi page render.
paper_style.style_consistency: Caption placement, sparse table rules and blue chart family are consistent; screenshots/case panels introduce Arial/Calibri/Comic Sans-like typography and saturated status colors, making the appendix intentionally heterogeneous but less typographically uniform.

caption.text: Figure 1 Illustration of challenges of geometric interleaved reasoning on several sub-tasks between SFT-Text only and SFT-Interleaved, which can only be tackled by RL post-training.

Cong. & Simi. 68.57/67.14/80.36; Quad. & Polygons 63.64/64.29/74.03. Descriptive accuracies only; no sample sizes or uncertainty.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2 Illustration of Faire framework. The model generates a reasoning trace and GeoGebra code from a geometry problem. As for reward designs, a gated reward enforces answer correctness Cans and code executability Cexe, then aggregates perceptual Cperc, semantic Csem, and formal verification signals Cgeo.

color.semantic_mapping: Pastel blocks partition problem, model loop, render, verifier signals, reward accumulation and RL loss; red marks the loss endpoint.

encodings.line: Arrows and loop indicate state flow.
encodings.text: Labels Cans, Cexe, Cperc, Csem, Cgeo, Reward Score Accumulation and L_GRPO.

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual interface only: a geometry problem enters a VLM that emits reasoning and GeoGebra code, rendering feeds answer/code/perceptual/semantic/formal checks, and a gated reward feeds GRPO. No sample statistics or uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: 将摘要中的 functional alignment 具体化为 text → code → rendered state → verifier → reward；p. 5 的 verifier 定义、Table 4 的组件消融和 Appendix C Figures 9–11 是该接口的展开。
design_strengths: 生成、执行、三视角检查和优化边界在一张图中可追踪。
回环箭头表达构图会参与后续推理。
design_weaknesses: 节点、箭头和嵌入图较密，字号偏小。
颜色同时承担模块和状态语义，失败分支未完整画出。
figures.reusable_pattern: 对具有可执行中间状态的方法，在一张图中固定生成、验证和优化的输入/输出边界。

caption.text: Figure 3 The data construction pipeline employing a tri-perspective verification mechanism—Visual Alignment, Semantic Consistency, and Geometric Assertion—to curate rigorous interleaved geometric reasoning samples.

figures.data_and_statistics: Pipeline has no throughput values: Gemini generation is followed by Visual Alignment, Semantic Consistency and Geometric Assertion checks, then manual screening and All-Pass retention. Table 1 reports the resulting split composition.
figures.evidence_relation: 连接 §4 的合成/过滤叙述与 Table 1 的 split statistics；三条过滤器分别在 Figure 2 和 Appendix C Figures 9–11 中获得 reward/prompt 解释。
design_strengths: 三条过滤通道按错误类型分离，输入和 checker 输出可见。
终点明确指向训练数据。
design_weaknesses: 没有各过滤器通过率、拒绝量或人工筛查成本。
嵌入截图和多重箭头使阅读方向需要反复定位。

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty; split-level descriptive percentages only.
tables.data_and_statistics: Columns are row label, SFT, RL and Eval. Rows: Instances 4643/2321/1025; Plane geometry 51.5%/51.6%/54.7%; Function 29.4%/28.3%/27.4%; Analytic geometry 19.1%/20.1%/17.9%; Hard difficulty 54.4%/54.8%/54.1%; ≥2 images 39.6%/38.4%/43.6%. Percentages use the corresponding split as denominator.
tables.evidence_relation: Together with Figure 3 and Figure 4 it defines the Faire-Bench evaluation base used by Tables 2–5.
design_strengths: Compact and consistent one-decimal split comparison.
Minimal rules keep the small table legible.
design_weaknesses: No total column or absolute category counts.
Caption does not define the ≥2 images criterion.
tables.reusable_pattern: Place split counts and key composition percentages in one small, no-vertical-rule table.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2 Main results on interleaved geometry reasoning. Acc: answer accuracy. Verification uses tri-perspective scores: Parser (vsem), Code (vform), Judge (vvis). Similarity metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-L/chrF; PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) report surface matching to references.

tables.uncertainty: No error bars, intervals or seed variation; Avg is the mean of Parser, Code and Judge verification views.
tables.data_and_statistics: Model rows are Gemma3-12B, Kimi-VL-A3B, InternVL3.5-8B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, GLM-4.1V-9B, Qwen3-VL-8B, GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, Gemini-2.5-Pro, GPT-5.2 and Faire. Columns are Acc; BLEU/ROUGE-L/chrF; PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS; Parser/Code/Judge/Avg. Faire is 74.82, 25.06, 46.75, 55.57, 14.79, 65.10, 52.76, 37.27, 60.39, 38.44, 45.37. Gemini-2.5-Pro has highest Acc 78.24 but Avg 19.86. GPT-5.2 has PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS 9.85/43.79/69.23, Parser 7.02 and Avg 24.62. Qwen3-VL-8B has verification 8.62/25.47/10.47/14.85.
tables.evidence_relation: Headline decision surface: separates answer correctness and reference-surface matching from functional verification. Figures 1 and 5–8 provide mechanism/cases; Tables 4–5 provide ablations; Figure 12/Table 7 give appendix slices.
design_strengths: Grouped header puts surface and functional metrics on the same decision surface.
Cyan Faire row and green best cells make the intended comparison visible.
design_weaknesses: Many metrics have no explicit direction arrows or cost column.
Color highlighting, uncertainty and sample/seed details are absent.
tables.reusable_pattern: When the claim concerns usable intermediate states, place answer, surface and functional metrics together but keep their definitions separate.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3 Results on GenExam. Math-Str: structural correctness; Math-Rel: relational correctness.

tables.data_and_statistics: Columns Model, Math-Rel and Math-Str. Rows are Emu3 11.3/0.0, Janus-Pro 13.7/0.0, Qwen-Image 18.9/0.0, Imagen-4-Ultra 35.9/2.6, Gemini-2.5-Image 43.1/0.7, GPT-Image-1 52.0/8.0 and Faire 52.3/9.3 (Math-Rel/Math-Str).
tables.evidence_relation: Tests transfer beyond geometry by separating relational plausibility from structural correctness; complements Figures 6/15 without replacing Table 2.
design_strengths: Only three columns and a clear structure/relations contrast.
Faire is visibly best on Math-Str while matching the best Math-Rel.
design_weaknesses: Metric units and denominators are not in the table.
One small transfer table cannot establish broad generalization.
tables.reusable_pattern: Separate relational correctness from structural correctness in adjacent columns and define abbreviations in the caption.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4 Reward ablation (leave-one-out). Executability-only RL provides limited gains; Faire requires all verifiers to achieve functional alignment.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, seed variation or compute column.
tables.data_and_statistics: Columns Model, Acc and Draw Avg. Rows: Faire (Full) 74.83/45.37; Faire w/o Alignment 66.53/38.31; Faire w/o Semantic 66.24/39.37; Faire w/o Geo Assert 65.88/37.15; RL (Exec-only) 64.29/35.65; SFT (Interleaved) 62.48/35.23. Leave-one-out removes one verifier at a time; Exec-only and SFT are separate controls.
tables.evidence_relation: Directly tests the Figure 2/3 reward components and the claim that no single executable signal replaces the three complementary verifiers; Table 5 isolates training regime.
design_strengths: Full, leave-one-out and weak controls share the same columns.
Row order follows the ablation logic.
design_weaknesses: Draw Avg is not defined in the header.
No variance, seed or cost information.
tables.reusable_pattern: Keep complete method, one-component removals and weak controls together to avoid conflating no verifier with no RL.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5 Ablation on Training Paradigms. Comparing the interplay between drawing and solving. Note that while drawing initially hurts SFT accuracy, it boosts performance post-RL.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty; Text-only Draw is shown as — because it is not applicable.
tables.data_and_statistics: Two-factor cross table: Paradigms × SFT (Acc %, Draw) × RL (Acc %, Draw). Text-only: SFT 68.13/— and RL 71.21/—. Interleaved: SFT 62.48/35.23 and RL 74.83/45.37. The table isolates the SFT drop and RL reversal.
tables.evidence_relation: Minimal quantitative replay of Figure 1; with Table 4 it closes the training-paradigm × reward-design evidence chain.
design_strengths: 2×2 factors are explicit and the em dash avoids treating non-applicable Draw as zero.
Compact enough for the main text.
design_weaknesses: Only two rows and no repetitions or seed information.
Draw is not given a unit or aggregation definition in the header.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a crossed factor table when the claim depends on an interaction rather than four unrelated model rows.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6 Comparison with existing multimodal math benchmarks. We contrast capability coverage (solving, drawing, interleaved solving) and supervision modality (text, image, code).

tables.uncertainty: Binary capability/modality indicators; no numerical uncertainty.
tables.data_and_statistics: Columns Benchmark, Solving, Drawing, Interleaved, Text, Image and Code. MathVista, MathVerse, MM-MATH, MathScape, GeoEval, WE-MATH, MMSCIBench, PolyMath and SOLIDGEO are Solving/Text/Image ✓ and otherwise ✗; MATH2VISUAL adds Drawing ✓; GGBench has Drawing/Text/Image/Code ✓ but Solving/Interleaved ✗; Faire-Bench has all six capabilities/modalities ✓.
tables.evidence_relation: Positions Faire-Bench relative to representative multimodal math benchmarks and motivates why Figure 3 uses aligned text/image/code; Table 7 then evaluates GGBench process stages.
design_strengths: Binary matrix reveals the scarcity of interleaved/code supervision quickly.
Header dimensions are easy to scan.
design_weaknesses: Capability criteria and evidence sources are not in the table.
Common ✓ entries may hide input/difficulty differences.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a capability × supervision matrix for benchmark positioning, with explicit rules for each binary category.

tables.label: Table 7

caption.text: Table 7 Results on GGBench. Stage-wise interleaved evaluation (higher is better) and image similarity (lower LPIPS is better).

tables.uncertainty: No error bars, intervals or seed variation; missing stage values are em dashes, not zero.
tables.evidence_relation: Decomposes the appendix E claim into planning/middle/final process and surface similarity; it complements Figure 12 category breadth and grounds the text claim that Faire leads overall and in the middle process.
design_strengths: Two-level headers include directions and scaling factors.
Row groups separate UMMs and LLMs/LRMs; em dash preserves missingness.
design_weaknesses: Many narrow columns and long model names reduce readability.
Heterogeneous metrics and no uncertainty/cost require careful interpretation.
tables.reusable_pattern: Group process stages and image similarity in one appendix table, showing direction and scale in each metric header.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes the SFT paradox; Figures 2–3 specify method and dataset gates; Figure 4/Table 1 establish corpus composition; Table 2 is the main answer/surface/functional comparison; Figures 5–8 give mechanism, qualitative, transfer and human-alignment evidence; Figures 9–17 and Tables 6–7 provide verifier prompts, category/process slices and cases.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions start with a numbered object title, then give setup/comparison or interface role. Table 2 and Table 7 define metric groups/directions relatively well; Figures 8 and 12 are terse and omit sample/scale details. Case captions state the intended finding but not the single-case boundary.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables use multi-level grouped headers for heterogeneous metrics (Tables 2 and 7), crossed factors for training interactions (Table 5), and binary capability columns for benchmark positioning (Table 6). Minimal horizontal rules and mostly consistent decimal precision are used throughout.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2/3 verifier and filter interfaces map to Table 2 Parser/Code/Judge, while Table 4 removes each verifier and Table 5 isolates the training-regime interaction. This makes a mechanism→outcome→ablation chain, but no seed/variance or matched-compute isolation supports a strong causal attribution.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main text keeps the headline comparison, two cases and compact ablations; Appendix C publishes the three prompts, D provides category heatmap, E decomposes GGBench stages, and F gives five additional construction cases. Figure 12 is a late float on page 24 but retains stable numbering/caption linkage.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Main prose/tables use Computer Modern objects, while embedded diagrams and prompts use mixed sans/rounded families including Arial, Calibri and Comic Sans-like text. The distinction is visible and functional but not uniform.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue remains the statistical base color and red signals failure/loss; green/orange/blue bands consistently separate verifier or construction roles. Check/cross and direct labels provide some redundancy, but several charts still rely primarily on hue.

most_reusable_patterns: Use a single pipeline to expose text→executable construction→tri-perspective verification→reward boundaries.
Place answer accuracy, surface similarity and functional verification in one grouped main table with separate definitions.
Use leave-one-out and crossed-factor tables to distinguish reward components from training-regime interactions.
Make qualitative panels show problem, reasoning, rendered state and error analysis together, then publish verifier prompts and process/category slices in the appendix.
highest_value_objects: Table 2 as the headline decision surface.
Figure 2 as the method interface overview.
Figures 6–7 and 16–17 as concrete text–diagram mismatch evidence.
Figure 12 and Table 7 as category/process breadth checks.
failure_patterns: Most performance objects omit uncertainty, sample size, seeds and cost.
Figure 8 omits human-evaluation protocol; Figure 12 omits category denominators and color-scale explanation.
Dense case/prompt panels use small mixed-font screenshots; Figure 1/5/8 rely on color or trend styling with limited grayscale redundancy.
The public repository provides rendered PNGs but no editable plotting/table source, so exact style and reproduction parameters remain unavailable.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Blue statistical charts and sparse tables establish the performance spine, while colorful executable-construction pipelines and dense qualitative cases make the claim that diagrams are proof-carrying reasoning states visually concrete.
